title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. The goal is to provide a single reference for employees and people managers to ensure consistent, auditable, and compliant behavior across the company.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors with access to company systems or data.
- Excludes partner-managed systems where an explicit written exception is recorded in the vendor contract.

Owners and escalation paths
- Policy owner: People Ops (primary)
- Technical owner (access controls / RBAC): Security & Compliance
- Procurement and vendor contracts: Finance & Legal
- Travel and expenses: Finance Ops
- Escalation contact: people-ops@redwood.example.com; security@redwood.example.com; procurement@redwood.example.com

1) Access and permissions
- Principle: least privilege by default. Access is role-based and reviewed quarterly.
- Roles and groups: maintain canonical role definitions in /confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth. Common roles: viewer, contributor, engineer, infra-admin, security-admin, finance, hr-admin.
- Onboarding flow (numbered):
  1. Hiring manager submits access bundle via onboarding form (link to template).
  2. People Ops approves and notifies Security to provision cloud/SSO groups.
  3. Security provisions SSO groups and issues MFA enrollment.
  4. Employee completes required training (security basics & data handling) within 7 days.
- Offboarding flow (emergency and regular):
  - Emergency: People Ops immediately triggers access revocation using the offboard runbook; Security confirms within 30 minutes.
  - Standard: Access revoked on employee termination date; manager confirms deprovisioning in 48 hours.
- Privileged access: Break-glass / just-in-time (JIT) provisioning required for infra-admin and security-admin roles. All JIT sessions must be logged and approved, and elevated sessions require a 2nd approver (security or engineering manager).
- Quarterly access review: Managers receive a roster to certify access; non-responders are escalated to People Ops.

2) Change management
- Scope: changes to production services, critical infra, security controls, and data handling systems.
- Classification:
  - Minor change: configuration-only with no user-visible impact and <15 min deploy window. Requires peer review and CI pipeline gating.
  - Standard change: feature or infra change with planned window, has rollback plan and runbook, requires manager approval and staging validation.
  - Major change: architecture changes, database schema changes, or anything requiring maintenance window or cross-team coordination. Requires change advisory board (CAB) sign-off.
- Change window: standard maintenance windows occur Saturdays 02:00-06:00 UTC unless otherwise approved. Emergency changes: must follow emergency change procedure and be documented in the post-deploy review.
- CAB: meets weekly; members include SRE, eng-infra, product owner, security, and a People Ops representative when changes impact access.
- Change checklist (required on the ticket): rollback steps, blast radius, monitoring playbook, owners, and post-change validation steps.

3) Data management
- Classification: Public, Internal, Confidential, Regulated (PII/PHI). Owners must tag datasets and services with classification.
- Storage and encryption: Confidential and Regulated data must be encrypted at rest and in transit; keys managed through company KMS (see /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging).
- Retention: default retention for Internal data is 3 years; Confidential and Regulated retention must follow contractual/legal obligations and be approved by Legal.
- Backup policy: critical production data must have daily backups with 30-day hot retention and 1-year archived retention for regulated datasets unless contract states otherwise.
- Data access requests:
  1. Initiator files a data access request with justification and minimal scope.
  2. Data owner and Security review; Legal reviews for regulated datasets.
  3. Approved access provisioned with time-limited credentials and audited.
- Data handling and transfer: all transfers of Regulated data outside approved environments require DPA/contract addendum and must use encrypted channels and approved vendor endpoints.

4) Procurement and expenses
- Thresholds and approvals:
  - <= $2,000: manager approval.
  - $2,001- $25,000: department head + Finance Ops approval.
  - > $25,000: VP-level approval + Finance & Legal review.
- Purchase process (cloud infra and SaaS):
  1. Submit a procurement request via the procurement system with justification, cost-center, and expected contract term.
  2. Procurement evaluates vendor security questionnaire and routing to Legal if needed.
  3. Finance issues PO or processes card payment after approvals.
- Corporate card and expenses: receipts required for all expenses. Expense reports must be submitted within 30 days. Per-diem and mileage follow the company travel policy.
- Budget reserve: teams must notify Finance if a recurring SaaS cost will exceed 15% of the team's quarterly budget.

5) Vendor management and onboarding
- Vendor classification: Strategic, Standard, One-time. Strategic vendors require an annual review and executive sponsor.
- Onboarding checklist:
  - Complete vendor intake form.
  - Security questionnaire + SOC2 / ISO27001 or compensating controls.
  - Contract review by Legal (include Data Processing Addendum if vendor processes personal data).
  - Assign vendor owner and ensure onboarding runbook is documented.
- Periodic reviews: Service performance, security posture, and cost reviews at cadence: Strategic (quarterly), Standard (annually).
- Offboarding vendors: revoke all access, rotate keys, recover data, confirm deletion/return per contract clauses, and close the vendor record in procurement system.

6) Travel policy (high level)
- Booking: employees should use the company travel portal or approved travel vendor for all trips.
- Pre-approval: trips over $2,000 require manager and Finance sign-off.
- Per-diem and lodging: follow limits published in the travel policy template (domestic per-diem $75/day; international varies by country-see template).
- Expense submission: submit receipts within 30 days of trip completion. Lost-receipt policy: provide a signed lost-receipt form and manager approval for amounts under $75.
- Safety and emergency: register travel with Security for trips to high-risk locations; Security provides a contact and evacuation guidance.

7) Internal templates and forms (quick index)
- Onboarding access request (link to template)
- Offboard checklist (link to runbook)
- Procurement request form (link)
- Vendor intake and security questionnaire (link)
- Travel pre-approval and expense template (link)
- Change request checklist / CAB submission template (link)

Appendix: Audit, compliance and enforcement
- Audits: People Ops, Security, and Finance will run annual cross-functional audits on access, procurement, vendor controls, and expense compliance. Results are reported to the executive risk committee.
- Non-compliance: violations of these policies may result in access suspension, disciplinary action, or contract consequences for vendors. Exceptions require documented approvals from People Ops and the relevant policy owner.

How to use this document
- Use the templates linked in section 7 for requests. If you need an exception, file an exception request with People Ops and include justification and mitigations.
